children: , the networking and cybersecurity infrastructure leader, said AI agents already consume roughly 60% of global inference capacity. Their token usage has surged fourteenfold since February, while Cisco shares gained approximately 0.3% to $109.59 Wednesday.

The company delivered $17.3 billion in fiscal fourth-quarter revenue, an 18% increase powered by a 28% jump in networking sales. AI-infrastructure orders from hyperscalers hit $4 billion for the quarter and $9.3 billion for the full year. Management's most striking number: AI agents require about 450% more network bandwidth than people completing similar tasks.

Those annual AI orders represent nearly 14.7% of Cisco's $63.3 billion in fiscal-year revenue, though orders do not immediately become sales. The picture shows the shares trading 47.6% above their GF Value estimate of $74.25, signaling that investors already expect substantial AI-driven growth. Cisco has the traffic boom it wanted; now it must convert that demand into revenue quickly enough to outrun rising memory costs and pressure from its hardware-heavy sales mix.

title: Cisco Says AI Agents Now Consume 60% of Global Inference
